guides.trackerIntro: Scan the car with WAiNK before you take it. The scan shows its tracker type and registration fee. A yellow tracker can be cleared in Chapter 3. A red one needs a later unlock from Randy.
guides.trackerUnlock: When the shop accepts the car
guides.standardEffect: You can drive the car, but modifications require registration.
guides.advancedEffect: Slow down and the tracker can report your location to the police.
guides.standardUnlock: After Moses texts you in Chapter 3
guides.advancedUnlock: After Randy calls about advanced trackers
guides.advancedHeading: How to remove an advanced tracker in GTA 6
guides.advancedBody: Work through Randy’s Wish List and his special vehicle requests, including the ’64 Declasse Mamba GT. Wait for his call confirming that Pay ’n’ Spray can service cars with advanced trackers. Lose any active pursuit, then take the red-tracker car to a shop and pay to register it.
guides.standardHeading: How to remove a standard tracker
guides.standardBody: Complete Welcome to Vice City in Chapter 3 and read Moses’s text about Pay ’n’ Spray. Bring the yellow-tracker car to the shop and register it. Buying a respray alone leaves the tracker active.
guides.registerHeading: How to register a car at Pay ’n’ Spray
guides.registerBody: Check the fee in WAiNK and free up a garage space. Drive into the shop once the pursuit ends, open Services, choose Register and confirm the price. Choose Sell only if you want to hand over the car for cash.
guides.immobilizerHeading: What does the Tracker Immobilizer unlock?
guides.immobilizerBody: Players use “Tracker Immobilizer” for the service Randy unlocks at Pay ’n’ Spray. Once he calls, the shop can register a car carrying a red tracker. Until you register that car, driving fast only delays its next police alert.
guides.spoilerBody: This guide covers reported chapter titles, settings, story beats, and mission lists. Read the overview first if you want to avoid spoilers.

guides.chaptersIntro: Explore the five reported GTA 6 chapters, their settings, and local checklists. Use this as a planning aid, not an official mission database.
guides.chaptersAnswerTitle: How many GTA 6 chapters are there?
guides.chaptersAnswerBody: GamesRadar's reported list contains 94 mission entries across five chapters, including three optional entries. That is 91 entries when optional missions are excluded. These are secondary-source counts, not official Rockstar counts, and other launch summaries vary.
guides.ch2Setting: Paradise Lost — Leonida and the transition into prison
guides.ch3Setting: Tits, Ass, Drug Money — Vice City crime and Randy
guides.ch4Setting: Vice City, Baby — Vice City and late-game robberies
guides.ch5Setting: Top of the World, Ma — the final escalation
guides.countBody: The chapter totals are 22, 13, 27, 25, and 7. Chapter 3 includes one optional entry, and there are three optional entries across the five reported lists. Chapter 4's final title is redacted by GamesRadar; secondary sources call it From Zero. The 94-entry total is therefore not a count of required missions or an official Rockstar total.
guides.tipBody: Follow the current in-game mission flow if a report is wrong. Keep optional jobs separate, do not treat redacted names as confirmed, and remember that progress is local only.
guides.chaptersMoneyBody: Story and repeatable payouts are tracked separately in the money guide. Chapter 3 has several reported repeatable activities; Chapter 4 has reported repeatable bank-vault work.
guides.chaptersCharactersBody: Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos lead the story. Mandy appears during early rent collection, while contacts such as Moses and Randy connect to reported repeatable content.
guides.chapter3Intro: Chapter 3 is reported as Tits, Ass, Drug Money. It moves into Vice City crime, introduces more repeatable opportunities, and connects with Randy's car wishlist. GamesRadar lists 27 entries, including one optional mission.
guides.chapter3Unlocks: Continue the main story through the preceding chapters until the current mission flow points you to Chapter 3. No fixed mission number is promised because reports and optional jobs can affect progression.
guides.chapter4Intro: Chapter 4 is reported as Vice City, Baby, with Vice City robberies and late-game escalation. GamesRadar lists 25 entries. Its final title is redacted in that report; secondary sources call it From Zero, so this guide does not present that name as Rockstar-confirmed.
guides.chapter4Unlocks: Finish the main Chapter 3 story progression and continue with the missions the game offers. Entry conditions are kept broad rather than inventing a fixed cutscene or mission number.
guides.charactersIntro: A concise guide to the leads, supporting cast, and repeatable contacts. Roles are separated from performer credits, and uncertain details are left out.
guides.castNoteBody: Named performer credits here come from Rockstar's credits. Role labels describe this guide's grouping; fan casting and unsupported claims are not treated as credits.
guides.charJasonBio: Jason Duval is one of GTA VI's two leads. A former soldier, he is trying to settle into a quieter life in Leonida.
guides.charLuciaBio: Lucia Caminos is the other lead. Her story begins after release from prison as she resists pressure to return to a life of crime.
guides.charBrianBio: Brian Heder is a supporting character in Vice City. His property connects him with Jason and his tenant, Mandy.
guides.charCalBio: Cal Hampton is a supporting character associated with Jason and Lucia's world. Official trailer material presents him as a paranoid hacker.
guides.charDonnieBio: Donnie is a supporting figure connected to the lead duo's criminal world. His guide category does not imply a larger story role than sources establish.
guides.charBoobieBio: Boobie Ike is part of the supporting cast around Jason and Lucia. This guide avoids assigning him unverified affiliations or plot details.
guides.charDrequanBio: Dre'Quan is a supporting character in the GTA VI cast. Public material places him within the story's wider criminal-world context.
guides.charBaeBio: Bae-Luxe is a supporting character connected to the GTA VI story. Keep her role distinct from the repeatable contact category used for Moses, Tyrone, Yasmani, and Randy.
guides.charRoxyBio: Roxy is a supporting character in the GTA VI cast. No additional biography is inferred from fan speculation.
guides.charRaulBio: Raul is a supporting character in the GTA VI story. His listing here reflects the cast role, not a claim about mission frequency.
guides.charMandyBio: Mandy is Brian Heder's tenant. Jason meets her during early Pipework rent collection. Lexie Shoaibi provides her voice and motion capture.
guides.charMosesBio: Moses is a repeatable contact tied to reported Chapter 2 vehicle hand-ins. The activity and its payout are secondary-source reports, not official guarantees.
guides.charTyroneBio: Tyrone is listed as a repeatable or contact role. His repeatable content is kept separate from the reported main-story mission totals.
guides.charYasmaniBio: Yasmani is listed as a repeatable or contact role. Check the current in-game contact menu for available activities rather than assuming a fixed schedule.
guides.charRandyBio: Randy is a repeatable contact whose reported Chapter 3 wishlist covers 18 cars. Secondary sources report about $30,000+ for each clean car, subject to current availability.
guides.charactersMandyBody: Mandy's relationship to Brian Heder, her early rent-collection scene, and Lexie Shoaibi's credit are confirmed guide facts. Claims that she is a serial killer are unconfirmed fan theory.
guides.charactersChaptersBody: Use the chapter guide to follow the reported story order. Repeatable contacts can appear alongside that progression, but their activities are not added to official mission counts.
guides.mandyIntro: Mandy is a supporting character connected to Brian Heder's property and Jason's early rent collection. This page separates confirmed context from a popular fan theory.
guides.mandySpoiler: Spoiler warning: this page discusses early-story events and details behind the Mandy theory.
guides.mandyAnswerTitle: Is Mandy a serial killer in GTA VI?
guides.mandyAnswerBody: That has not been established by Rockstar. The fan theory draws on a finger bone, a person-sized hole, and acid barrels, but those clues do not confirm a serial-killer identity or any other conclusion.
guides.mandyFact1: Mandy is a supporting character, not one of the two leads.
guides.mandyFact2: She is a tenant of Brian Heder.
guides.mandyFact3: Jason meets her during early Pipework rent collection.
guides.mandyFact4: Lexie Shoaibi is credited for Mandy's voice and motion capture.
guides.mandyFact5: Her confirmed early appearance gives fans material for theory-building, not proof of hidden motives.
guides.mandyTheoryBody: Fans point to a finger bone, a person-sized hole, and acid barrels as possible clues. Together they form an unconfirmed serial-killer theory; this guide does not promote it to canon.
guides.mandyUnknown1: Rockstar has not confirmed that Mandy is a serial killer.
guides.mandyUnknown2: The theory does not establish who owns or caused the evidence fans cite.
guides.mandyUnknown3: It is unclear whether those details are intentional clues, atmosphere, or something else.
guides.mandyPopularityBody: Mandy's brief early appearance and unsettling story details invite close reading. Her popularity is discussed qualitatively here; no unsupported poll ranking or audience number is claimed.
guides.mandyCastBody: Rockstar credits Lexie Shoaibi for Mandy's voice and motion capture. Keep that credit separate from the unconfirmed claims about the character.
guides.moneyIntro: Compare reported GTA 6 money methods, story payouts, and repeatable activities. Amounts are approximate secondary-source reports, not guaranteed rewards.
guides.moneyScopeBody: This guide covers console-gameplay money context, not a PC port. It provides no game files, cracks, private servers, or T3 code, and it does not verify live repeatability after patches.
guides.moneyBankBody: BuckMe is the game's bank. Bank funds are distinct from carried cash, so do not describe a payout as banked unless the current game flow actually deposits it.
guides.moneyCashBody: Carried cash is capped at $20,000 and is lost on death. Plan large earnings around the risk of carrying them rather than assuming death preserves your wallet.
guides.moneyLootBody: Some early-game loot-respawn loops are player-reported. Respawn behavior and values can change with patches, so a loop is not treated as reliably repeatable here.
guides.moneyMethodsIntro: The table separates unlock context, payout estimates, and status. Repeatable means reported as repeatable, not live-verified by this site. Story payouts happen once.
guides.moneyM6Unlock: Chapter 4 · armored truck · four-star wanted level
guides.moneyVaultBody: Secondary sources report repeatable Chapter 4 vault robberies with an armored truck and a four-star wanted level, paying up to about $205,000. Treat that ceiling as an estimate and expect changes rather than promising a live route.
guides.moneyGlitchBody: Glitches and exploits can corrupt saves, trigger bans, or cause online-mode issues. Early loot respawns are player-reported, unverified, and may be patched. This site does not test or endorse live exploit routes.
guides.moneyCheatTitle: Is there a confirmed money cheat?
guides.moneyCheatBody: No reliably confirmed money cheat code is available in the sources used for this guide. Do not trust videos or sites that present an unverified code as fact.
guides.moneyOrderBody: First follow the story, including the Chapter 3 completion payout. Then use currently available repeatable contacts such as Moses, paint shops, jewelry robberies, and Randy. Treat Chapter 4 vaults and all glitches as patch-sensitive.
guides.moneyPcTitle: Does this describe a PC port?
guides.moneyPcBody: No. PC-port keywords are limited to what the status and checker pages support. This money guide is not a PC-port page and makes no claim about PC availability or port features.
guides.moneyFaq1Q: What is the fastest reported way to make money?
guides.moneyFaq1A: The largest reported repeatable ceiling is the Chapter 4 bank-vault method at up to about $205,000, but it is high-risk and patch-sensitive. Earlier options include Randy's clean-car deliveries and repeatable robberies.
guides.moneyFaq2Q: Is carried cash the same as BuckMe money?
guides.moneyFaq2A: No. Carried cash is capped at $20,000 and lost on death. BuckMe is the bank; only funds actually deposited there should be treated as banked.
guides.moneyFaq3Q: Should I use a money glitch or cheat code?
guides.moneyFaq3A: Avoid relying on them. Glitches may damage saves, cause bans, or affect online play, and no reliably confirmed money cheat code is documented here.
guides.moneyFaq4A: No. They are approximate secondary-source reports. Unlock conditions, repeatability, loot values, and availability may change with the current build or patch.
guides.chapter1Intro: Follow the opening chapter from the Prologue to Discharge Time. The published list counts 22 entries, including the opening sequence.
guides.chapter1Unlocks: Pipework appears seventh, before the introduction of Buck Me. If you are tracking completion, leave a slot for entry 18: the source hides its title to protect a story reveal.
guides.chapter2Intro: This chapter has 13 listed entries. Two are optional, which explains why a required-story count can show eleven.
guides.chapter2Unlocks: Moses appears early in the chapter. Near the end, Thrillbillies and Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab are marked optional. Checking Out closes the chapter before the move into Chapter 3.
guides.chapter5Intro: Seven entries make this the shortest of the five reported chapters. Use the final two positions to track the ending without revealing its title.
guides.chapter5Unlocks: The chapter follows Vice City, Baby. Protective Custody is entry six. One final story entry follows it; GamesRadar withholds that name, so reaching the sixth entry still leaves the finale ahead.

requirements.intro: Compare your desktop GPU with the graphics class of PS5 and Xbox Series X while official GTA VI PC requirements are pending.
requirements.answerTitle: Are official GTA 6 PC requirements available?
requirements.answer: No. As checked on 2026-11-24, Rockstar's official release and platform pages list PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. They do not provide an official PC release date, CPU, GPU, RAM, VRAM, storage, or operating-system requirement.
requirements.officialBody: Not announced. No values in this table are official PC requirements.
requirements.forecastBody: Base PS5 has a 10.3 TFLOPS GPU and Series X a 12 TFLOPS GPU. Digital Foundry tested the RX 6700 against PS5. We use that card as a broad desktop anchor for the pair. Individual games, drivers and memory bandwidth can change the order.
requirements.resolutionBody: 1080p, 1440p, and 4K selections describe your target only. Without a resolution-specific benchmark model, the site does not claim a qualitative tier or FPS at any resolution.
requirements.laptopBody: A laptop GPU name does not reveal TGP, cooling, or sustained performance. Integrated graphics use shared memory, which is not equivalent to dedicated VRAM. These factors remain Unknown.
requirements.evidenceBody: Official and community evidence are labeled separately. Hardware specifications link to manufacturer pages. If an official profile becomes available, it must be versioned and reviewed without silently rewriting historical results.
requirements.cpuEstimate: Both consoles use an eight-core Zen 2 CPU. Ryzen 7 3700X is a desktop architecture reference.
requirements.ramEstimate: 16 GB shared between CPU and GPU on both consoles. A 16 GB PC RAM minimum cannot be inferred.
requirements.storageEstimate: SSD in both consoles. PC install size unconfirmed.
requirements.bandsTitle: Which desktop cards fall in each band?
requirements.bandsBody: The bands are editorial estimates. In the older 1080p Ultra raster suite we treat cards within roughly 20% of RX 6700 as near. For newer cards we use overlapping desktop models such as RTX 4060 to place them in a broad class.

status.intro: The official PC version has not been announced. This page tracks verifiable release and platform statements without inventing dates.
status.answer: No official PC release has been identified. Rockstar's official release page states that GTA VI became available on 2026-11-19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. That does not prove a PC version will never be released; it means no PC date can be claimed now.
status.platformsBody: PS5 and Xbox Series X|S are listed. Windows, Linux, macOS, and PC specifications are not listed.
status.releaseBody: GTA VI launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
status.leonidaTitle: Leonida is not an official PC release
status.leonidaBody: The unofficial project has no verified playable build and unavailable upstream pages. It should not be treated as Rockstar's PC release.
status.uncertaintyBody: We do not claim a PC date, port progress, benchmark result, or future platform plan. Absence of an announcement is not proof of permanent cancellation.
status.initialNews: Take-Two named PS5 and Xbox Series X|S in the first announcement. Its original 2025 window applied to consoles.
status.latestNews: The official GTA VI page still lists PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. A Windows release date has yet to be announced.

support.methodologyIntro: The checker is a transparent reference-matching tool, not a game benchmark. It keeps availability, hardware evidence, and performance claims separate.
support.methodStep1: Stable hardware IDs, device types, ranges, enums, and source references are checked. Missing fields stay null. Unknown hardware is never guessed from budget, age, core count, or memory capacity.
support.methodStep2: GTA 6 official PC status and Leonida playability come from status files. A capable PC cannot change those facts.
support.methodStep3: CPU and GPU benchmark ratios require the same dataset, unit, and a positive reference value. Null, mismatched, or stale evidence returns Unknown. Production records currently contain no performance benchmarks.
support.methodStep4: RAM, VRAM, OS, architecture, storage, and Vulkan are reported separately. Exact historical model matches are labeled as stale community references and do not establish playability.
support.methodStep5: The bands are editorial estimates. In the older 1080p Ultra raster suite we treat cards within roughly 20% of RX 6700 as near. For newer cards we use overlapping desktop models such as RTX 4060 to place them in a broad class.
support.dataCoverage: {cpus} CPU records and {gpus} GPU records, including desktop and laptop variants. Manufacturer specification links are stored for every record. Performance scores are intentionally null.
support.limitations: Browser GPU renderer strings can be masked, RAM is approximate, CPU model and disk details are not reliably exposed, laptop TGP varies, and Vulkan runtime features cannot be verified. External sources can become stale or unavailable.
support.sourcePolicy: Manufacturer pages support identity and specifications only. No benchmark database is copied. PassMark data is not used. Community values remain labeled and stale when their source cannot be revalidated.
support.privacyIntro: This policy explains how VI Ready at canirungta6.online handles information. The core checker runs in your browser, does not require an account, and remains usable when analytics is blocked.
support.privacyScope: VI Ready is an independent informational website and is not affiliated with Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive. This policy covers this website, generated share links and images, local browser storage, site analytics, hosting request metadata, and email sent to the published support address. It does not cover third-party websites or services that you choose to visit.
support.privacyLocal: Hardware selections, detected hints, checklist progress, and calculations are processed in your browser. Versioned localStorage can retain selected hardware IDs, enum values, RAM, VRAM override, free-space input, and whitelisted chapter mission IDs. Raw DxDiag files, machine names, serial numbers, WebGL renderer strings, and device fingerprints are not saved by the site.
support.privacyShare: Share URLs contain only whitelisted configuration parameters needed to reproduce a check. faq.question: Can I run GTA 6 on PC now?
faq.answer: An official PC release has not been announced. Hardware readiness cannot make an unannounced version available.

faq.question: Why does the checker return Unknown?
faq.answer: Unknown is used when official requirements, a compatible benchmark, or a required input is missing. It is more accurate than inventing a score.

faq.question: Does the browser detect my full PC?
faq.answer: No. It may detect a masked GPU renderer, logical thread count, approximate memory, and limited OS hints. CPU model, disk, and Vulkan features require manual confirmation.

faq.question: Can laptop graphics match desktop graphics?
faq.answer: Not reliably. Laptop power limits and cooling can change sustained performance, so desktop and laptop variants stay separate.

faq.question: Is shared memory the same as VRAM?
faq.answer: No. Integrated graphics share system memory. Shared capacity is not reported as dedicated VRAM.

faq.question: Will a matching result show FPS?
faq.answer: No. P0 never displays FPS without reproducible game benchmarks. Reference matching is not a gameplay test.

faq.question: Is Leonida playable?
faq.answer: No verified playable build was identified. Its recorded project and repository pages were unavailable during the latest check.

faq.question: Are these official Rockstar requirements?
faq.answer: No. This is an independent site. Official facts, community history, and unavailable forecasts are labeled separately.
